diagnoses.why: Muscarinic blockade producing dryness, which is the discriminating feature
diagnoses.mimic: Sympathomimetic toxidrome → diaphoretic rather than dry

diagnoses.name: Digoxin toxicity
diagnoses.why: Sodium-potassium ATPase inhibition producing both the arrhythmia and the potassium shift
diagnoses.mimic: Hyperkalemia from other causes → no visual symptoms, no characteristic arrhythmia

diagnoses.name: Beta blocker or calcium channel blocker overdose
cluster: with hyperglycemia pointing to calcium channel blockade
diagnoses.why: Both cause bradycardia and hypotension; glucose separates them, since beta blockade tends to hypoglycemia
diagnoses.mimic: Digoxin toxicity → bradycardia with hyperkalemia and characteristic ectopy

diagnoses.name: Serotonergic drug interaction
cluster: with clonus greater in the legs
diagnoses.why: Onset within hours of a drug change, with lower-limb-predominant clonus
diagnoses.mimic: Malignant hyperthermia → follows an anesthetic trigger, with masseter spasm

diagnoses.name: Methemoglobinemia
cluster: Acute cyanosis with a saturation gap and chocolate-brown blood not correcting on oxygen
diagnoses.why: Hemoglobin locked in the ferric state, so oxygen does not help and the blood color changes
diagnoses.mimic: Shunt physiology → cyanosis without a saturation gap or abnormal blood color

diagnoses.name: Psoriasis, plaque
cluster: well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale and nail pitting
diagnoses.why: Extensor distribution with sharp borders and nail change, the mirror image of eczema
diagnoses.mimic: Atopic dermatitis → flexural, ill-defined, lichenified, intensely pruritic

diagnoses.name: Atopic dermatitis
cluster: lichenified plaques with a personal or family atopic history
diagnoses.why: Itch-scratch cycle in flexures, producing thickening rather than scale
diagnoses.mimic: Psoriasis → extensor, sharply demarcated, silvery scale

diagnoses.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
cluster: flaccid bullae with Nikolsky positivity and prominent mucosal erosions
diagnoses.why: Intraepidermal split from desmoglein antibodies, so blisters are flaccid and mucosa is involved early
diagnoses.mimic: Bullous pemphigoid → tense bullae, mucosa usually spared, older patient

diagnoses.name: Bullous pemphigoid
cluster: tense bullae on urticarial plaques in an older patient
diagnoses.why: Subepidermal split, so blisters are tense and roof-intact
diagnoses.mimic: Pemphigus vulgaris → flaccid bullae with mucosal disease

diagnoses.name: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
cluster: medication-induced with a 1 to 3 week latency
diagnoses.why: Widespread keratinocyte apoptosis with mucosal involvement, timed to a new drug
diagnoses.mimic: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome → mucosa spared, superficial split, young child

diagnoses.name: Erythema multiforme
diagnoses.why: True targets with three concentric zones on hands and feet
diagnoses.mimic: Urticaria multiforme → transient annular wheals, individual lesions under 24 hours

diagnoses.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
cluster: rapidly enlarging painful ulcer with a violaceous undermined border and pathergy
diagnoses.why: Neutrophilic dermatosis, so trauma worsens it and debridement is harmful
diagnoses.mimic: Infected ulcer → responds to antibiotics, no undermined violaceous edge

diagnoses.name: Melanoma
diagnoses.why: Change over time in an asymmetric pigmented lesion is the discriminating feature
diagnoses.mimic: Seborrhoeic keratosis → stuck-on, waxy, symmetric, stable

diagnoses.name: Basal cell carcinoma
cluster: slowly enlarging pearly papule with telangiectasia and a rolled border on sun-exposed skin
diagnoses.why: Very slow local growth without metastasis, on cumulative sun damage
diagnoses.mimic: Squamous cell carcinoma → faster, keratotic, may be tender, can metastasize

diagnoses.name: Scabies
cluster: with burrows in finger webs and household contacts affected
diagnoses.why: Nocturnal itch with linear burrows and a contact history is close to specific
diagnoses.mimic: Atopic dermatitis → flexural, no burrows, no contact clustering

diagnoses.name: Erythroderma
cluster: generalized erythema involving over 90% of the skin
diagnoses.why: Extent itself becomes the problem, causing fluid and temperature loss regardless of cause
diagnoses.mimic: Extensive drug eruption → under 90%, no thermoregulatory compromise

diagnoses.name: Cutaneous drug eruption, morbilliform
cluster: 4 to 14 days after a new drug
diagnoses.why: Timing to drug exposure with sparing of mucosa and organs
diagnoses.mimic: DRESS → facial edema, eosinophilia, hepatitis, longer latency

diagnoses.name: Compartment syndrome
cluster: pain out of proportion to exam with pain on passive stretch and a tense compartment
diagnoses.why: Rising compartment pressure, where pain and passive stretch precede pulselessness
diagnoses.mimic: Deep vein thrombosis → no pain on passive stretch, no compartment tension

diagnoses.name: Hip fracture
cluster: unilateral inability to weight bear with a shortened externally rotated leg after a fall
diagnoses.why: Mechanical discontinuity producing a characteristic limb position
diagnoses.mimic: Hip contusion → able to weight bear, no deformity, normal radiograph

diagnoses.name: Osteoarthritis
cluster: activity-related joint pain with brief gelling and bony enlargement
diagnoses.why: Worse with use and better with rest, the mirror image of inflammatory arthritis
diagnoses.mimic: Rheumatoid arthritis → inflammatory, morning stiffness over an hour, symmetric small joints

diagnoses.name: Rotator cuff tear
cluster: activity-related shoulder pain with weakness on external rotation and a positive drop arm
diagnoses.why: Structural tendon failure producing weakness rather than only pain
diagnoses.mimic: Adhesive capsulitis → restricted passive as well as active range

diagnoses.name: Adhesive capsulitis
cluster: progressive shoulder stiffness with equally restricted active and passive range
diagnoses.why: Capsular contracture limits passive movement, which tendon disease does not
diagnoses.mimic: Rotator cuff tear → passive range preserved

diagnoses.name: Lumbar disc herniation
cluster: radicular leg pain in a dermatome with a positive straight leg raise
diagnoses.why: Root compression producing dermatomal pain with a reproducible tension sign
diagnoses.mimic: Spinal stenosis → neurogenic claudication relieved by flexion, bilateral

diagnoses.name: Lumbar spinal stenosis
cluster: progressive neurogenic claudication relieved by sitting or leaning forward
diagnoses.why: Canal narrowing that eases when the spine flexes, unlike vascular claudication
diagnoses.mimic: Vascular claudication → relieved by standing still, absent pulses

diagnoses.name: Septic bursitis
cluster: localized swelling over a bursa with overlying erythema and preserved joint range
diagnoses.why: Infection confined to the bursa, so the joint itself moves normally
diagnoses.mimic: Septic arthritis → joint range severely restricted and painful

diagnoses.name: Osteoporotic vertebral fracture
cluster: midline thoracolumbar pain after minimal trauma with focal tenderness and loss of height
diagnoses.why: Fragility fracture, so the mechanism is trivial relative to the injury
diagnoses.mimic: Malignant infiltration → night pain, constitutional features, lytic lesion

diagnoses.name: Achilles tendon rupture
cluster: and absent plantarflexion on calf squeeze
diagnoses.why: Complete tendon discontinuity abolishes the Thompson test
diagnoses.mimic: Achilles tendinopathy → activity-related pain with an intact Thompson test

diagnoses.name: Cauda equina from disc
diagnoses.why: Compression of multiple lumbosacral roots, a time-critical surgical emergency
diagnoses.mimic: Unilateral radiculopathy → no saddle involvement, no sphincter disturbance

diagnoses.name: Osteomyelitis, diabetic foot
cluster: indolent ulcer with probe-to-bone positivity and raised inflammatory markers
diagnoses.why: Contiguous spread from an overlying ulcer, so the ulcer precedes the bone disease
diagnoses.mimic: Neuropathic ulcer without osteomyelitis → probe-to-bone negative, normal markers

diagnoses.name: Deep vein thrombosis
cluster: unilateral leg swelling with calf tenderness and a measured circumference difference over 3 cm
diagnoses.why: Unilaterality plus measurement, since bilateral swelling points systemic
diagnoses.mimic: Cellulitis → erythema and warmth predominate, fever more common

diagnoses.name: Acute limb ischemia
diagnoses.why: Sudden arterial occlusion producing the six-P sequence within hours
diagnoses.mimic: Critical limb ischemia → chronic, rest pain over weeks, collaterals present

diagnoses.name: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
diagnoses.why: Rupture producing pain plus shock plus a palpable expansile mass together
diagnoses.mimic: Renal colic → colicky, hemodynamically stable, stone on imaging

diagnoses.name: Superficial thrombophlebitis
cluster: with a tender palpable cord along a superficial vein and localized erythema
diagnoses.why: Thrombosis of a superficial vein, so the cord is palpable and linear
diagnoses.mimic: Cellulitis → diffuse rather than linear, no palpable cord

diagnoses.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
cluster: bilateral dependent edema with hemosiderin staining and medial malleolar ulceration
diagnoses.why: Venous hypertension over years producing pigmentation and a characteristic ulcer site
diagnoses.mimic: Arterial ulcer → lateral or distal, punched out, painful, absent pulses

diagnoses.name: Lymphedema
cluster: nonpitting limb swelling with a positive Stemmer sign and skin thickening
diagnoses.why: Protein-rich interstitial fluid, so it does not pit and the skin thickens
diagnoses.mimic: Venous edema → pitting, improves overnight, pigmentation rather than thickening

diagnoses.name: Carotid stenosis
cluster: or transient monocular visual loss and contralateral hemispheric symptoms
diagnoses.why: Territorial symptoms match the vessel, which is why the eye and the opposite hemisphere pair
diagnoses.mimic: Vertebrobasilar disease → bilateral or posterior symptoms, no monocular loss

diagnoses.name: Takayasu arteritis
diagnoses.why: Large-vessel inflammation in a young patient, so pulses and pressures differ between limbs
diagnoses.mimic: Atherosclerotic disease → older, no constitutional features, normal inflammatory markers

diagnoses.name: Anaphylaxis
cluster: with airway compromise and hypotension after an exposure
diagnoses.why: Two or more organ systems within minutes of a trigger, which no other reaction does
diagnoses.mimic: Vasovagal syncope → bradycardic, pallor without urticaria, rapid spontaneous recovery

diagnoses.name: Hereditary angiedema
cluster: nonpruritic angiedema without urticaria and unresponsive to antihistamines
diagnoses.why: Bradykinin-mediated, so there is no urticaria and no response to antihistamine or adrenaline
diagnoses.mimic: Histaminergic angiedema → urticarial, pruritic, responds to antihistamine

diagnoses.name: Chronic spontaneous urticaria
cluster: recurrent wheals with individual lesions resolving under 24 hours and no identified trigger
diagnoses.why: Duration of the individual lesion is the discriminator, not the duration of the illness
diagnoses.mimic: Urticarial vasculitis → lesions lasting over 24 hours, bruising, burning rather than itching

diagnoses.name: Drug-induced anaphylactoid reaction
cluster: clinically identical to anaphylaxis but without prior sensitization
diagnoses.why: Direct mast cell activation, so it can occur on first exposure
diagnoses.mimic: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis → requires prior sensitization

diagnoses.name: Common variable immunodeficiency
cluster: recurrent sinopulmonary infection with low immunoglobulins and poor vaccine response
diagnoses.why: Antibody failure producing encapsulated organism infection and bronchiectasis over years
diagnoses.mimic: Cystic fibrosis → sweat chloride positive, pancreatic insufficiency, earlier onset

diagnoses.name: Mastocytosis
cluster: and hypotension with a raised baseline tryptase
diagnoses.why: Mast cell burden producing paroxysmal mediator release between attacks
diagnoses.mimic: Carcinoid syndrome → flushing with diarrhea and raised urinary 5-HIAA

diagnoses.name: Bronchiolitis
cluster: polyphonic wheeze in an infant under 2 with coryza
diagnoses.why: Small airway inflammation in infancy, so wheeze follows a viral prodrome at a specific age
diagnoses.mimic: Asthma → recurrent, older child, bronchodilator responsive

diagnoses.name: Croup
cluster: inspiratory stridor with a barking cough and low-grade fever
diagnoses.why: Subglottic edema, so stridor is inspiratory and the cough is characteristic
diagnoses.mimic: Epiglottitis → toxic, drooling, no barking cough, hyperacute

diagnoses.name: Bacterial tracheitis
diagnoses.why: Purulent membrane in the trachea, so it fails croup treatment and looks septic
diagnoses.mimic: Croup → responds to adrenaline and steroid, not toxic

diagnoses.name: Intussusception
cluster: colicky abdominal pain in an infant with drawing up of legs and redcurrant jelly stool
diagnoses.why: Telescoped bowel producing paroxysmal pain with intervening calm
diagnoses.mimic: Gastroenteritis → constant discomfort, no pain-free intervals, no mass

diagnoses.name: Pyloric stenosis
cluster: projectile vomiting at 3 to 6 weeks with a hypochloremic alkalosis
diagnoses.why: Gastric outlet obstruction proximal to the ampulla, so vomit has no bile
diagnoses.mimic: Gastroesophageal reflux → nonprojectile, thriving, no alkalosis

diagnoses.name: Malrotation with volvulus
cluster: bilious emesis in a neonate with abdominal distension
diagnoses.why: Bile in the vomit of a newborn implies obstruction distal to the ampulla
diagnoses.mimic: Duodenal atresia → double bubble on radiograph, no whirl sign

diagnoses.name: Kawasaki disease
cluster: febrile for five days with conjunctival injection
diagnoses.why: A defined cluster over a defined duration, with coronary risk if untreated
diagnoses.mimic: Scarlet fever → sandpaper rash, positive throat culture, no conjunctivitis

diagnoses.name: Henoch-Schonlein purpura
cluster: palpable purpura on the buttocks and legs with arthralgia
diagnoses.why: IgA small-vessel vasculitis with a characteristic dependent distribution in a child
diagnoses.mimic: Immune thrombocytopenia → nonpalpable petechiae, low platelets

diagnoses.name: Acute epiglottitis, pediatric
cluster: with muffled voice and no cough
diagnoses.why: Supraglottic swelling threatening the airway, distinguished by absence of cough
diagnoses.mimic: Croup → barking cough present, less toxic, gradual

diagnoses.name: Neonatal sepsis, early onset
diagnoses.why: Vertical transmission, so timing and maternal history are the discriminators
diagnoses.mimic: Transient tachypnea of the newborn → resolves in 48 hours, no systemic features

diagnoses.name: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
cluster: oxygen dependence beyond 36 weeks corrected age in a preterm infant
diagnoses.why: Defined by persistent oxygen requirement at a corrected gestational threshold
diagnoses.mimic: Recurrent aspiration → episodic desaturation tied to feeds

diagnoses.name: Febrile seizure, simple
cluster: generalized seizure under 15 minutes with fever
diagnoses.why: Defined by duration, generalization, age, and single occurrence
diagnoses.mimic: Meningitis → focal features, prolonged, or persistently altered afterward

diagnoses.name: Developmental dysplasia of the hip
cluster: asymmetric skin creases with limited abduction and a positive Ortolani in infancy
diagnoses.why: Instability detectable before ambulation, so the exam precedes symptoms
diagnoses.mimic: Septic hip → acute, febrile, refusal to move the limb

diagnoses.name: Transient synovitis of the hip
diagnoses.why: Reactive effusion without infection, so the child is well and afebrile
diagnoses.mimic: Septic arthritis of the hip → febrile, unable to weight bear, raised inflammatory markers

diagnoses.name: Perthes disease
cluster: painless limp in a child aged 4 to 8 with limited internal rotation
diagnoses.why: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head, slow and initially painless
diagnoses.mimic: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis → older, obese, acute or chronic groin pain

diagnoses.name: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
cluster: obese adolescent with hip or referred knee pain and an externally rotated limb
diagnoses.why: Physeal slip in a growth spurt, and knee pain referred from the hip is the trap
diagnoses.mimic: Perthes disease → younger, painless limp

diagnoses.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis, pediatric first presentation
cluster: Subacute polyuria and weight loss then acute vomiting
diagnoses.why: New type 1 diabetes presenting in crisis, so the prodrome precedes the decompensation
diagnoses.mimic: Gastroenteritis → no polyuria, no acidosis, normal glucose

diagnoses.name: Congenital hypothyroidism
diagnoses.why: Detected by newborn screening before signs, which is why screening exists
diagnoses.mimic: Neonatal jaundice, physiologic → resolves by 2 weeks, thyroid tests normal

diagnoses.name: Cystic fibrosis
diagnoses.why: Exocrine failure across lung and pancreas simultaneously, from infancy
diagnoses.mimic: Primary ciliary dyskinesia → situs inversus in half, normal sweat chloride

diagnoses.name: Non-accidental injury
cluster: Injuries inconsistent with the mechanism given
diagnoses.why: The inconsistency and the multiplicity of ages are the finding, not any one injury
diagnoses.mimic: Osteogenesis imperfecta → blue sclerae, family history, characteristic bone density

diagnoses.name: Frailty syndrome
diagnoses.why: A measurable phenotype of reduced reserve, independent of any single disease
diagnoses.mimic: Sarcopenia alone → muscle loss without the exhaustion and activity criteria

diagnoses.name: Polypharmacy adverse event
cluster: or hypotension after a prescribing change
diagnoses.why: Temporal link to a medication change, and the drug list is the diagnostic test
diagnoses.mimic: Progressive dementia → no temporal link, does not improve on deprescribing

diagnoses.name: Orthostatic hypotension in the elderly
cluster: orthostatic dizziness with a documented systolic fall over 20 mmHg on standing
diagnoses.why: Measured rather than reported, and often delayed beyond one minute
diagnoses.mimic: Vasovagal syncope → prodromal nausea and pallor, not reproducible on standing

diagnoses.name: Falls, multifactorial
diagnoses.why: Multifactorial by definition, so single-cause explanations under-treat it
diagnoses.mimic: Mechanical single fall → identifiable trip, no recurrence, normal gait

diagnoses.name: Pressure injury
cluster: over a bony prominence in an immobile patient
diagnoses.why: Sustained pressure over bone, so location predicts it better than any host factor
diagnoses.mimic: Moisture-associated dermatitis → diffuse, not over a prominence, no depth

diagnoses.name: Elder mistreatment
cluster: and caregiver control of the interview
diagnoses.why: Pattern of inconsistency plus social dynamics rather than any single injury
diagnoses.mimic: Accidental injury → consistent mechanism, timely presentation

diagnoses.name: Urinary incontinence, urge
cluster: with urgency preceding leakage and frequent small volumes
diagnoses.why: Detrusor overactivity, so urgency precedes rather than follows the leak
diagnoses.mimic: Stress incontinence → leakage on cough or exertion without urgency

diagnoses.name: Sarcopenia
cluster: progressive loss of muscle mass and strength with slow gait speed
diagnoses.why: Measurable by grip and gait speed, and separable from weight loss alone
diagnoses.mimic: Cachexia → inflammatory, with weight loss and catabolic drive

diagnoses.name: Late-life depression
cluster: and cognitive slowing that improves with treatment
diagnoses.why: Reversible cognitive impairment accompanying mood, historically called pseudodementia
diagnoses.mimic: Alzheimer disease → progressive, does not reverse with antidepressant

diagnoses.name: Postoperative delirium
diagnoses.why: Time-locked to the operation and fluctuating, unlike a dementia baseline
diagnoses.mimic: Baseline dementia → chronic, stable attention, no acute change

diagnoses.name: Osteoporotic fragility fracture
cluster: Acute fracture after a fall from standing height or less
diagnoses.why: Fracture disproportionate to the force, which defines fragility
diagnoses.mimic: High-energy fracture → mechanism explains the injury

diagnoses.name: Advanced care planning mismatch
cluster: life-limiting illness with treatment intensity discordant from stated goals
diagnoses.why: Not a disease but a recognizable failure state worth naming on rounds
diagnoses.mimic: Undocumented preferences → goals never established rather than contradicted

diagnoses.name: Septic shock
cluster: vasodilated with warm peripheries and lactic acidosis
diagnoses.why: Distributive physiology, so the patient is warm and vasodilated despite hypotension
diagnoses.mimic: Cardiogenic shock → cold peripheries, raised filling pressures, low cardiac output

diagnoses.name: Cardiogenic shock
cluster: with elevated JVP and pulmonary edema
diagnoses.why: Pump failure, so filling pressures are high and the periphery is shut down
diagnoses.mimic: Hypovolemic shock → flat JVP, responds to volume

diagnoses.name: Hypovolemic shock
cluster: hypotensive with a flat JVP and a rapid response to volume
diagnoses.why: Reduced preload, so the neck veins are empty and fluid works
diagnoses.mimic: Distributive shock → warm, vasodilated, fluid-refractory

diagnoses.name: Obstructive shock
cluster: hemodynamically unstable with elevated JVP and clear lungs
diagnoses.why: Mechanical obstruction to filling or outflow, so the JVP is high while the lungs stay dry
diagnoses.mimic: Cardiogenic shock → pulmonary edema present

diagnoses.name: Neurogenic shock
cluster: hypotensive and bradycardic after spinal cord injury
diagnoses.why: Loss of sympathetic tone, so hypotension occurs without compensatory tachycardia
diagnoses.mimic: Hemorrhagic shock → tachycardic, cold, clammy

diagnoses.name: Acute respiratory failure, type 1
cluster: hypoxemic with a widened A-a gradient and shunt physiology
diagnoses.why: Oxygenation failure from alveolar filling or collapse
diagnoses.mimic: Type 2 failure → hypercapnic with a normal gradient

diagnoses.name: Acute respiratory failure, type 2
cluster: hypercapnic with respiratory acidosis and reduced drive or pump
diagnoses.why: Ventilation failure, so carbon dioxide rises while the lung may be normal
diagnoses.mimic: Type 1 failure → hypoxemic with a widened gradient

diagnoses.name: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
cluster: febrile with new consolidative infiltrate after 48 hours of ventilation
diagnoses.why: Timing after intubation plus new infiltrate, distinguishing it from the admitting diagnosis
diagnoses.mimic: Atelectasis → resolves with recruitment, no fever or purulence

diagnoses.name: Abdominal compartment syndrome
cluster: distended tense abdomen with oliguria and rising airway pressures
diagnoses.why: Intra-abdominal pressure impairing both renal perfusion and ventilation simultaneously
diagnoses.mimic: Ileus → distension without oliguria or ventilatory compromise

diagnoses.name: Transfusion-related acute lung injury
cluster: bilateral infiltrates within 6 hours of transfusion
diagnoses.why: Timing to transfusion with normal filling pressures
diagnoses.mimic: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload → elevated JVP, responds to diuresis

diagnoses.name: Refeeding syndrome
cluster: after reintroduction of nutrition in a malnourished patient
diagnoses.why: Insulin-driven intracellular shift, so electrolytes fall as feeding starts
diagnoses.mimic: Sepsis → electrolytes not shifting in step with feeding

diagnoses.name: Propofol infusion syndrome
cluster: and bradyarrhythmia during prolonged high-dose infusion
diagnoses.why: Dose and duration dependent mitochondrial toxicity
diagnoses.mimic: Septic shock → responds to source control, no dose relationship

diagnoses.name: Critical illness polyneuromyopathy
cluster: flaccid weakness with failure to wean after prolonged critical illness
diagnoses.why: Acquired neuromuscular weakness, so weaning fails despite resolved lung disease
diagnoses.mimic: Guillain-Barré → albuminocytologic dissociation, preceding infection

diagnoses.name: Fat embolism syndrome
cluster: 24 to 72 hours after long bone fracture
diagnoses.why: A triad appearing after a latent interval following fracture
diagnoses.mimic: Pulmonary embolism → no petechial rash, no latency after fracture

diagnoses.name: Colorectal carcinoma, right-sided
cluster: with iron deficiency anemia and weight loss but no obstruction
diagnoses.why: Caecal tumors bleed occultly into a wide lumen, so anemia precedes bowel symptoms
diagnoses.mimic: Left-sided colorectal carcinoma → obstructive, altered bowel habit, visible blood

diagnoses.name: Colorectal carcinoma, left-sided
cluster: progressive change in bowel habit with hematochezia and narrowing stool
diagnoses.why: A narrow lumen obstructs early, so bowel symptoms precede anemia
diagnoses.mimic: Diverticular disease → episodic, no progressive habit change, no weight loss

diagnoses.name: Gastric adenocarcinoma
cluster: progressive epigastric pain with early satiety
diagnoses.why: Infiltrative growth restricting distensibility, hence early satiety
diagnoses.mimic: Peptic ulcer disease → episodic, fasting-related, responds to acid suppression

diagnoses.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
cluster: with a hypervascular lesion showing arterial enhancement and washout
diagnoses.why: The imaging phenotype in a cirrhotic liver is diagnostic without biopsy
diagnoses.mimic: Regenerative nodule → no arterial hyperenhancement or washout

diagnoses.name: Breast carcinoma
cluster: nontender mass with skin dimpling or nipple retraction
diagnoses.why: Fixation and skin change from desmoplastic tethering rather than the mass itself
diagnoses.mimic: Fibroadenoma → mobile, rubbery, well-circumscribed, younger

diagnoses.name: Inflammatory breast carcinoma
cluster: unilateral erythema with peau d'orange and no fever
diagnoses.why: Dermal lymphatic invasion mimicking infection but afebrile and antibiotic-unresponsive
diagnoses.mimic: Mastitis → febrile, painful, responds to antibiotics, lactating

diagnoses.name: Prostate carcinoma
diagnoses.why: Blastic rather than lytic metastases, which is close to specific in a man
diagnoses.mimic: Benign prostatic hyperplasia → smooth symmetrical enlargement, obstructive symptoms

diagnoses.name: Cervical carcinoma
cluster: postcoital bleeding with a friable cervical lesion in an unscreened patient
diagnoses.why: Contact bleeding from a friable exophytic lesion at the transformation zone
diagnoses.mimic: Cervical ectropion → benign, non-friable, no mass

diagnoses.name: Endometrial carcinoma
cluster: postmenopausal bleeding with a thickened endometrial stripe
diagnoses.why: Any postmenopausal bleeding is malignancy until excluded
diagnoses.mimic: Endometrial atrophy → thin stripe, no mass

diagnoses.name: Thyroid carcinoma, papillary
cluster: firm thyroid nodule with microcalcifications and cervical nodes
diagnoses.why: Nodal spread with a characteristic sonographic phenotype
diagnoses.mimic: Benign colloid nodule → spongiform, no microcalcification or nodes

diagnoses.name: Head and neck squamous carcinoma
cluster: progressive hoarseness or dysphagia with a nontender neck node in a smoker
diagnoses.why: Persistent unilateral symptoms beyond three weeks with a fixed node
diagnoses.mimic: Reactive lymphadenopathy → tender, mobile, resolves

diagnoses.name: Esophageal adenocarcinoma
cluster: Progressive solid-food dysphagia with reflux history and distal esophageal location
diagnoses.why: Barrett metaplasia progressing distally, so reflux history precedes dysphagia
diagnoses.mimic: Squamous carcinoma → proximal, smoking and alcohol, no reflux history

diagnoses.name: Glioblastoma
cluster: progressive focal deficit with headache and a heterogeneous ring-enhancing mass crossing the midline
diagnoses.why: Infiltrative growth across the corpus callosum, with necrotic ring enhancement
diagnoses.mimic: Cerebral abscess → central restricted diffusion, febrile, source elsewhere

diagnoses.name: Brain metastasis
diagnoses.why: Hematogenous seeding lodges at the junction, and edema exceeds lesion size
diagnoses.mimic: Primary glioma → solitary, infiltrative, less edema relative to size

diagnoses.name: Sarcoma, soft tissue
diagnoses.why: Deep, large, and growing, which separates it from benign lipomatous lesions
diagnoses.mimic: Lipoma → superficial, fat signal throughout, stable

diagnoses.name: Testicular germ cell tumor
cluster: painless firm testicular mass in a young man with raised tumor markers
diagnoses.why: Painless enlargement in a young man is malignant until proven otherwise
diagnoses.mimic: Epididymal cyst → separate from the testis, transilluminates

diagnoses.name: Cancer of unknown primary
cluster: Metastatic disease with no identifiable primary after standard imaging and endoscopy
diagnoses.why: Defined by the failure of a completed search, so tissue profiling replaces more imaging
diagnoses.mimic: Occult primary later found → identified on directed workup

diagnoses.name: Neuroendocrine tumor with carcinoid syndrome
cluster: Episodic flushing with secretory diarrhea and right-sided valvular disease
diagnoses.why: Vasoactive mediators reaching the systemic circulation past the liver
diagnoses.mimic: Mastocytosis → raised tryptase, urticaria pigmentosa, no valve disease

diagnoses.name: Acute cellular rejection
cluster: with graft dysfunction and lymphocytic infiltrate on biopsy
diagnoses.why: Cell-mediated attack on the graft, so biopsy shows lymphocytes and steroids work
diagnoses.mimic: Calcineurin inhibitor toxicity → high drug level, no infiltrate, improves on dose reduction

diagnoses.name: Antibody-mediated rejection
cluster: graft dysfunction with donor-specific antibodies and C4d deposition
diagnoses.why: Humoral mechanism, so the finding is complement deposition rather than infiltrate
diagnoses.mimic: Acute cellular rejection → C4d negative, steroid responsive

diagnoses.name: Chronic allograft nephropathy
cluster: progressive graft dysfunction with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy
diagnoses.why: Slow fibrotic decline rather than an inflammatory episode
diagnoses.mimic: Recurrent primary disease → original glomerular pattern returns on biopsy

diagnoses.name: Graft-versus-host disease, acute
diagnoses.why: Donor lymphocytes attacking three specific target organs together
diagnoses.mimic: Drug eruption → no liver or gut involvement, resolves on withdrawal

diagnoses.name: Graft-versus-host disease, chronic
diagnoses.why: Autoimmune-like fibrosing syndrome rather than the acute triad
diagnoses.mimic: Scleroderma → no transplant history, nailfold changes, autoantibodies

diagnoses.name: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder
diagnoses.why: EBV-driven proliferation under immunosuppression, often regressing on dose reduction
diagnoses.mimic: Rejection → graft-localized, no EBV viremia

diagnoses.name: CMV disease post-transplant
cluster: febrile with cytopenias and organ-specific involvement
diagnoses.why: Reactivation under immunosuppression with tissue-invasive disease
diagnoses.mimic: CMV viremia alone → no organ involvement, asymptomatic

diagnoses.name: Calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity
cluster: rising creatinine with high trough levels and bland sediment
diagnoses.why: Dose-related vasoconstriction, so it tracks the level and improves on reduction
diagnoses.mimic: Rejection → biopsy infiltrate, does not improve on dose reduction

diagnoses.name: Invasive aspergillosis in the immunocompromised
cluster: neutropenic with a halo sign progressing to an air crescent
diagnoses.why: Angioinvasion producing perilesional hemorrhage then cavitation on recovery
diagnoses.mimic: Bacterial pneumonia → responds to antibacterials, no halo sign

diagnoses.name: Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome
cluster: Paradoxical worsening after starting antiretroviral therapy
with rising CD4 and falling viral load
diagnoses.why: Recovery of immunity unmasking or worsening an existing infection
diagnoses.mimic: Treatment failure → viral load not suppressed, CD4 not rising

diagnoses.name: Heat stroke
diagnoses.why: Thermoregulatory failure with central nervous system dysfunction, unlike simple exhaustion
diagnoses.mimic: Heat exhaustion → normal mental state, temperature under 40

diagnoses.name: Accidental hypothermia
diagnoses.why: Cold-induced slowing across every system, with a characteristic ECG deflection
diagnoses.mimic: Myxedema coma → thyroid tests abnormal, does not rewarm alone

diagnoses.name: High-altitude pulmonary edema
cluster: with exertional dyspnea and patchy infiltrates
diagnoses.why: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction after a defined ascent interval
diagnoses.mimic: Pneumonia → febrile, purulent sputum, lobar

diagnoses.name: High-altitude cerebral edema
cluster: with ataxia and altered consciousness beyond simple mountain sickness
diagnoses.why: Ataxia is the earliest reliable sign and separates it from headache alone
diagnoses.mimic: Acute mountain sickness → headache and nausea without ataxia

diagnoses.name: Decompression sickness
cluster: within 24 hours of ascent from depth
diagnoses.why: Inert gas bubble formation, so the dive profile is the diagnostic history
diagnoses.mimic: Musculoskeletal strain → no temporal relation to diving, no rash

diagnoses.name: Drowning, submersion injury
cluster: hypoxemic with pulmonary edema after immersion
diagnoses.why: Surfactant washout and alveolar flooding, so hypoxemia dominates
diagnoses.mimic: Aspiration pneumonitis → no immersion history, dependent distribution

diagnoses.name: Electrical injury
cluster: and arrhythmia disproportionate to visible burn
diagnoses.why: Current travels through tissue, so internal injury exceeds surface appearance
diagnoses.mimic: Thermal burn → injury proportional to the visible surface

diagnoses.name: Snake envenomation
cluster: and sometimes neurotoxicity after a bite
diagnoses.why: Venom-specific syndrome combining local and systemic effects
diagnoses.mimic: Cellulitis from a bite → slower, no coagulopathy

diagnoses.name: Carbon monoxide exposure, occupational
cluster: Subacute headache and confusion in workers with a shared environment and normal oximetry
diagnoses.why: Cluster of affected people plus falsely normal saturation
diagnoses.mimic: Viral illness → no clustering by workplace, normal carboxyhemoglobin

diagnoses.name: Silicosis
cluster: upper-lobe predominant nodules with eggshell-calcified hilar nodes and dust exposure
diagnoses.why: Occupational exposure with a characteristic upper zone and nodal calcification
diagnoses.mimic: Sarcoidosis → no exposure history, no eggshell calcification

diagnoses.name: Asbestosis
cluster: basilar fibrosis with pleural plaques and a latency of decades
diagnoses.why: Pleural plaques mark exposure, and the latency is measured in decades
diagnoses.mimic: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis → no plaques, no exposure history

diagnoses.name: Lead poisoning
diagnoses.why: Enzyme inhibition producing a specific smear finding with motor-predominant neuropathy
diagnoses.mimic: Iron deficiency → no stippling, no neuropathy

diagnoses.name: Noise-induced hearing loss
cluster: high-frequency sensorineural loss with a notch at 4 kHz
diagnoses.why: The audiometric notch is close to specific for noise exposure
diagnoses.mimic: Presbycusis → sloping high-frequency loss without a notch

diagnoses.name: Hyponatremia, hypovolemic
cluster: hyponatremic with low urine sodium and a response to saline
diagnoses.why: Volume depletion driving ADH appropriately, so the kidney conserves sodium
diagnoses.mimic: SIADH → euvolemic, urine sodium above 30, worsens with saline

diagnoses.name: Hyponatremia, hypervolemic
cluster: hyponatremic with edema and low urine sodium in heart failure or cirrhosis
diagnoses.why: Low effective arterial volume despite total body overload, so the kidney is sodium-avid
diagnoses.mimic: SIADH → euvolemic, no edema, normal effective volume

diagnoses.name: Osmotic demyelination syndrome
cluster: 2 to 6 days after rapid sodium correction
diagnoses.why: A delayed complication timed to the rate of correction rather than the sodium itself
diagnoses.mimic: Central pontine infarct → immediate, vascular territory, no correction history

diagnoses.name: Hypernatremia
cluster: hypernatremic in a patient without access to water
diagnoses.why: Almost always a water deficit plus impaired access, not a sodium excess
diagnoses.mimic: Diabetes insipidus → dilute urine despite hypernatremia

diagnoses.name: Hypokalemia with metabolic alkalosis
cluster: with hypertension in aldosterone excess or normotension in diuretic use
diagnoses.why: Blood pressure separates the mineralocorticoid causes from the tubular ones
diagnoses.mimic: Bartter or Gitelman syndrome → normotensive, high urine chloride

diagnoses.name: Hyperkalemia, pseudo
cluster: with a hemolyzed sample or marked thrombocytosis in a well patient
diagnoses.why: An artifact of collection or cell lysis, so the ECG is normal
diagnoses.mimic: True hyperkalemia → peaked T waves, clinical context fits

diagnoses.name: Hypercalcemia, PTH-dependent
cluster: hypercalcemic with inappropriately normal or raised PTH
diagnoses.why: Failure of feedback suppression is the defining biochemical relationship
diagnoses.mimic: Malignant hypercalcemia → suppressed PTH, subacute, symptomatic

diagnoses.name: Hypocalcemia, post-surgical
diagnoses.why: Timing to surgery with neuromuscular irritability
diagnoses.mimic: Hypomagnesemia → refractory to calcium until magnesium replaced

diagnoses.name: Hypomagnesemia
cluster: with refractory hypokalemia and hypocalcemia that do not correct until magnesium is given
diagnoses.why: Magnesium is required for potassium and PTH handling, so it gates both
diagnoses.mimic: Isolated hypokalemia → corrects with potassium alone

diagnoses.name: Hypophosphatemia, refeeding
diagnoses.why: Insulin-driven intracellular shift timed to nutrition
diagnoses.mimic: Chronic phosphate depletion → gradual, no temporal link to feeding

diagnoses.name: Anion gap metabolic acidosis
cluster: with a raised anion gap corrected for albumin
diagnoses.why: Added acid rather than lost bicarbonate, and the gap points to the class of acid
diagnoses.mimic: Non-gap acidosis → bicarbonate loss, normal gap

diagnoses.name: Non-anion gap metabolic acidosis
cluster: separated by the urine anion gap
diagnoses.why: Bicarbonate loss, with the urine anion gap distinguishing renal from gastrointestinal
diagnoses.mimic: Renal tubular acidosis → positive urine anion gap

diagnoses.name: Respiratory acidosis, acute on chronic
cluster: hypercapnic with a pH lower than the bicarbonate would predict
diagnoses.why: Compensation lags acute change, so the pH reveals the acute component
diagnoses.mimic: Chronic compensated hypercapnia → near-normal pH with high bicarbonate

diagnoses.name: Mixed acid-base disorder
cluster: Compensation deviating from the predicted value for the primary disturbance
diagnoses.why: Deviation from predicted compensation is the only way to detect a second disorder
diagnoses.mimic: Simple disorder → compensation matches prediction

diagnoses.name: Thiamine deficiency, wet beriberi
cluster: high-output heart failure with peripheral edema in a malnourished or alcohol-dependent patient
diagnoses.why: High-output rather than low-output failure, reversing rapidly with thiamine
diagnoses.mimic: Dilated cardiomyopathy → low output, no rapid reversal

diagnoses.name: Vitamin C deficiency
diagnoses.why: Defective collagen producing a characteristic perifollicular pattern
diagnoses.mimic: Vasculitic purpura → palpable, no corkscrew hairs

diagnoses.name: Niacin deficiency
diagnoses.why: A triad affecting skin, gut, and brain simultaneously
diagnoses.mimic: Porphyria cutanea tarda → blistering, no diarrhea or dementia

diagnoses.name: Zinc deficiency
diagnoses.why: Periorificial distribution with alopecia is close to specific
diagnoses.mimic: Necrolytic migratory erythema → glucagonoma, raised glucagon

diagnoses.name: Vitamin D deficiency osteomalacia
diagnoses.why: Defective mineralization producing weakness and bone pain together
diagnoses.mimic: Polymyositis → raised creatine kinase, normal bone chemistry

diagnoses.name: Copper deficiency myeloneuropathy
cluster: often after bariatric surgery or zinc excess
diagnoses.why: Mimics B12 deficiency exactly but with normal B12 and low copper
diagnoses.mimic: B12 deficiency → low B12 and raised methylmalonic acid

diagnoses.name: Protein-energy malnutrition
diagnoses.why: Sustained negative balance producing measurable functional loss
diagnoses.mimic: Cachexia of malignancy → inflammatory drive, not reversed by feeding

diagnoses.name: Iron overload, hereditary hemochromatosis
diagnoses.why: Deposition across joints, pancreas, and liver simultaneously, with saturation the screening test
diagnoses.mimic: Secondary iron overload → transfusion history, normal HFE genotype

diagnoses.name: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome
cluster: hypercapnic in obesity with daytime somnolence and no other cause
diagnoses.why: Awake hypercapnia in obesity, distinguishing it from sleep apnea alone
diagnoses.mimic: Obstructive sleep apnea → normal daytime carbon dioxide

diagnoses.name: Bariatric surgery micronutrient deficiency
cluster: or copper deficiency years after malabsorptive surgery
diagnoses.why: Anatomy-determined deficiencies appearing on a predictable timeline
diagnoses.mimic: Celiac disease → positive serology, no surgical history

diagnoses.name: Marfan syndrome
diagnoses.why: Connective tissue defect affecting eye, skeleton, and aorta together
diagnoses.mimic: Homocystinuria → downward lens dislocation, thrombosis, intellectual disability

diagnoses.name: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
cluster: and arterial or hollow organ rupture
diagnoses.why: Fragility of vessels and viscera rather than joint hypermobility alone
diagnoses.mimic: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos → joint hypermobility without vascular rupture

diagnoses.name: Familial hypercholesterolemia
diagnoses.why: Tendon xanthoma plus family history plus an LDL level rarely reached otherwise
diagnoses.mimic: Polygenic hypercholesterolemia → no xanthomas, lower LDL, no clear inheritance

diagnoses.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
cluster: recurrent epistaxis with mucocutaneous telangiectasia and a family history
diagnoses.why: Recurrent bleeding from visible telangiectasia with autosomal dominant inheritance
diagnoses.mimic: Von Willebrand disease → mucosal bleeding without telangiectasia

diagnoses.name: Sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis
cluster: severe bone pain with a known hemoglobinopathy and a precipitant
diagnoses.why: Recurrent stereotyped painful episodes on a known genetic background
diagnoses.mimic: Osteomyelitis → febrile, focal, raised inflammatory markers

diagnoses.name: Acute intermittent porphyria
diagnoses.why: Severe pain with a soft abdomen and neurologic features, provoked by drugs
diagnoses.mimic: Surgical abdomen → peritoneal signs, imaging abnormality

diagnoses.name: G6PD deficiency
cluster: episodic hemolysis after an oxidant drug
diagnoses.why: Trigger-dependent intravascular hemolysis with a characteristic smear
diagnoses.mimic: Autoimmune hemolysis → positive direct antiglobulin test, no trigger

diagnoses.name: Hereditary spherocytosis
diagnoses.why: Membrane defect producing spherocytes with a negative antiglobulin test
diagnoses.mimic: Warm autoimmune hemolysis → spherocytes with a positive antiglobulin test

diagnoses.name: Wilson disease
diagnoses.why: Liver and basal ganglia affected together in a young person
diagnoses.mimic: Autoimmune hepatitis → no neurologic or corneal findings

diagnoses.name: Lynch syndrome
cluster: with early-onset colorectal and endometrial cancer and mismatch repair deficiency
diagnoses.why: Tumor spectrum plus early age plus microsatellite instability
diagnoses.mimic: Familial adenomatous polyposis → hundreds of polyps, APC mutation

diagnoses.name: Fabry disease
cluster: and left ventricular hypertrophy in a young adult
diagnoses.why: Multi-organ storage disease with a distinctive painful neuropathy in youth
diagnoses.mimic: Small-fiber neuropathy → no angiokeratoma, no renal or cardiac involvement
